claim: HER4 (ERBB4) carries out essential functions in the development and maintenance of the cardiovascular and nervous systems.
source: Human Epidermal growth factor Receptor 4 (HER4 or ERBB4) carries out essential functions in the development and maintenance of the cardiovascular and nervous systems.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about HER4 function.

claim: HER4 activation is regulated by a diverse group of extracellular ligands including the neuregulin (NRG) family and betacellulin (BTC).
source: HER4 activation is regulated by a diverse group of extracellular ligands including the neuregulin (NRG) family and betacellulin (BTC), which promote HER4 homodimerization or heterodimerization with other HER receptors.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about HER4 regulation.

claim: NRG family and BTC promote HER4 homodimerization or heterodimerization with other HER receptors.
source: HER4 activation is regulated by a diverse group of extracellular ligands including the neuregulin (NRG) family and betacellulin (BTC), which promote HER4 homodimerization or heterodimerization with other HER receptors.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about ligand effects.

claim: Important cardiovascular functions of HER4 are exerted via heterodimerization with HER2.
source: Important cardiovascular functions of HER4 are exerted via heterodimerization with its close homolog and orphan receptor, HER2.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about HER4 cardiovascular function.

claim: Structural insights into ligand-mediated HER4 activation have been limited to crystallographic studies of HER4 ectodomain homodimers in complex with NRG1β.
source: To date structural insights into ligand-mediated HER4 activation have been limited to crystallographic studies of HER4 ectodomain homodimers in complex with NRG1β.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a summary of prior structural work.

claim: The authors report cryo-EM structures of near full-length HER2/HER4 heterodimers bound to NRG1β and BTC.
source: Here, we report cryo-EM structures of near full-length HER2/HER4 heterodimers and full-length HER4 homodimers bound to NRG1β and BTC.
evidence: This is the primary finding stated in the abstract.

claim: The authors report cryo-EM structures of full-length HER4 homodimers bound to NRG1β and BTC.
source: Here, we report cryo-EM structures of near full-length HER2/HER4 heterodimers and full-length HER4 homodimers bound to NRG1β and BTC.
evidence: This is the primary finding stated in the abstract.

claim: The structures of HER2/HER4 heterodimers bound to NRG1β and BTC are nearly identical.
source: We show that the structures of the heterodimers bound to either ligand are nearly identical and that in both cases the HER2/HER4 heterodimer interface is less dynamic than those observed in structures of HER2/EGFR and HER2/HER3 heterodimers.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract based on structural comparison.

claim: The HER2/HER4 heterodimer interface is less dynamic than those observed in structures of HER2/EGFR and HER2/HER3 heterodimers.
source: We show that the structures of the heterodimers bound to either ligand are nearly identical and that in both cases the HER2/HER4 heterodimer interface is less dynamic than those observed in structures of HER2/EGFR and HER2/HER3 heterodimers.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract based on structural comparison.

claim: Full-length HER4 homodimers bound to NRG1β and BTC display more large-scale dynamics mirroring states previously reported for EGFR homodimers.
source: In contrast, structures of full-length HER4 homodimers bound to NRG1β and BTC display more large-scale dynamics mirroring states previously reported for EGFR homodimers.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract based on structural analysis.

claim: Multiple glycan modifications are present within HER4 ectodomains and are modeled for the first time in HER receptors.
source: Our structures also reveal the presence of multiple glycan modifications within HER4 ectodomains, modeled for the first time in HER receptors, that distinctively contribute to the stabilization of HER4 homodimer interfaces over those of HER2/HER4 heterodimers.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract based on structural analysis.

claim: Glycan modifications distinctively contribute to the stabilization of HER4 homodimer interfaces over those of HER2/HER4 heterodimers.
source: Our structures also reveal the presence of multiple glycan modifications within HER4 ectodomains, modeled for the first time in HER receptors, that distinctively contribute to the stabilization of HER4 homodimer interfaces over those of HER2/HER4 heterodimers.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract based on structural analysis.

claim: HER4 is a ubiquitously expressed receptor functioning in heart, mammary, and neural development.
source: HER4 is a ubiquitously expressed receptor functioning in heart, mammary, and neural development (Lemmon and Schlessinger, 2010; Yarden and Sliwkowski, 2001; Plowman et al., 1993; Muraoka-Cook et al., 2008; Gassmann et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Binding of extracellular growth factors leads to HER4 receptor homodimerization or heterodimerization with EGFR, HER2, or HER3.
source: Binding of extracellular growth factors leads to HER4 receptor homodimerization or heterodimerization with one of three other HER receptor family members, EGFR, HER2, or HER3, and subsequent activation of their intracellular kinase domains (Lemmon and Schlessinger, 2010; Yarden and Sliwkowski, 2001; Plowman et al., 1993).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: HER4 is the only HER receptor with documented growth inhibitory effect on cells.
source: While HER4 activation is linked to signaling pathways activated by other HER receptors, including Ras/MAPK and PI3K/Akt, HER4 is the only HER with documented growth inhibitory effect on cells (Muraoka-Cook et al., 2008; Sweeney and Carraway, 2000; Sweeney et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: HER4 is more commonly observed to be lost or downregulated in human cancers, in contrast to other HER receptors which are widely linked to oncogenesis.
source: Consistent with this observation, and in contrast to other HER receptors for which genetic alterations are widely linked to oncogenesis (Arteaga and Engelman, 2014), HER4 is more commonly observed to be lost or downregulated in human cancers (Muraoka-Cook et al., 2008; Arteaga and Engelman, 2014; Naresh et al., 2006; Segers et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: HER4-activating mutations and overexpression have been observed in lung, melanoma, and gastric cancers.
source: More rarely, HER4-activating mutations and overexpression have been observed in lung, melanoma, and gastric cancers (Segers et al., 2020; Prickett et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Aberrant activation of HER4 is associated with neurological diseases including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), schizophrenia, and other psychological disorders.
source: Aberrant activation of HER4 is associated with neurological diseases including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), schizophrenia, and other psychological disorders, where inhibitory missense mutations in HER4, and either increased or decreased levels of the HER4 ligand NRG1, can lead to various disease phenotypes (Mei and Nave, 2014; Takahashi et al., 2013; Song et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: HER4 heterodimerization with HER2 is particularly important for cardiomyocyte survival under acute stress conditions.
source: In cardiomyocytes, HER4 heterodimerization with HER2 is particularly important for survival under acute stress conditions (Plowman et al., 1993; Bersell et al., 2009; Lee et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: HER2 and HER4 signaling are both essential for embryonic and postnatal heart development.
source: HER2 and HER4 signaling are both essential for embryonic and postnatal heart development (Gassmann et al., 1995; Lee et al., 1995; Odiete et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: HER2 does not undergo ligand-induced homodimerization and relies on HER4 for activation as an orphan receptor.
source: As an orphan receptor, HER2 does not undergo ligand-induced homodimerization and relies on HER4 for activation (Tzahar et al., 1996; Wallasch et al., 1995) when HER4 is bound to NRG1 produced by the cardiac endothelium (Odiete et al., 2012; Figure 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Disruption of the HER2/HER4 signaling has been attributed to the cardiotoxic effects of HER2-targeting cancer therapeutics, such as Herceptin.
source: Disruption of the HER2/HER4 signaling has been attributed to the cardiotoxic effects of HER2-targeting cancer therapeutics, such as Herceptin (Albini et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: The ectodomains of all HER receptors comprise four domains (I-IV).
source: The ectodomains of all HER receptors comprise of four domains (I-IV), which in the ligand-free state in EGFR, HER3, and HER4 adopt a tethered conformation around a beta hairpin protrusion known as the dimerization arm (Ferguson et al., 2003; Bouyain et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: In the ligand-free state, EGFR, HER3, and HER4 adopt a tethered conformation around the dimerization arm.
source: The ectodomains of all HER receptors comprise of four domains (I-IV), which in the ligand-free state in EGFR, HER3, and HER4 adopt a tethered conformation around a beta hairpin protrusion known as the dimerization arm (Ferguson et al., 2003; Bouyain et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Ligand binding between extracellular domains I and III causes a substantial conformational change that exposes the dimerization arm in domain II.
source: Early crystal structures of HER4/NRG1β, EGFR/EGF and EGFR/TGFα ectodomain (ECD) homodimers revealed that ligand binding between extracellular domains I and III causes a substantial conformational change that exposes the dimerization arm in domain II, allowing for the formation of active dimers stabilized through dimerization arm exchange between the monomers (Figure 1a; Garrett et al., 2002; Ferguson, 2008; Liu et al., 2012; Ogiso et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The orphan HER2 adopts an extended conformation in its apo state, thus being dimerization-competent without ligand binding.
source: The orphan HER2 adopts an extended conformation in its apo state, thus being dimerization-competent without ligand binding (Tzahar et al., 1996; Cho et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: HER2 does not form stable homodimers under physiological expression levels and relies on heterodimerization with another ligand-bound HER receptor for activation.
source: However, HER2 does not form stable homodimers under physiological expression levels and relies on heterodimerization with another ligand-bound HER receptor for activation (Tzahar et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: When complexed with NRG1β-bound HER3, HER2 fails to engage the HER3 dimerization arm leaving only the HER2 arm engaged at the dimer interface.
source: When complexed with NRG1β-bound HER3, HER2 fails to engage the HER3 dimerization arm leaving only the HER2 arm engaged at the dimer interface (Diwanji et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: Deletion of the HER3 dimerization arm does not impact HER2/HER3 dimerization and signaling.
source: The dispensability of the HER3 arm at the interface is corroborated by the observation that its deletion does not impact HER2/HER3 dimerization and signaling (Diwanji et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: In the EGF-bound EGFR/HER2 structure, the EGFR dimerization arm binds HER2 in a non-canonical manner characterized by increased dynamics.
source: In the EGF-bound EGFR/HER2 structure, the EGFR dimerization arm binds HER2 but in a non-canonical manner characterized by increased dynamics and interactions of the arm with HER2 domains II and III instead of domain II and I observed in most other HER ECD dimers.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: The dimerization arm of the HER2 partner receptor is not required for heterodimerization and activation in HER2/EGFR complexes.
source: As in the HER2/HER3 complex, the dimerization arm of the HER2 partner (in this case EGFR) is not required for heterodimerization and activation (Bai et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: HER2-containing heterodimer structures reveal a dynamic mode with which HER2 engages a dimerization arm from a partner receptor.
source: Together, the HER2-containing heterodimer structures reveal a dynamic mode with which HER2 engages a dimerization arm from a partner receptor (Diwanji et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: A strong preference for EGFR homodimerization is observed over heterodimerization with HER2 upon EGF treatment in cells expressing EGFR and HER2.
source: This is consistent with repeated findings in cells expressing EGFR and HER2 in which a strong preference for EGFR homodimerization is observed over heterodimerization with HER2 upon EGF treatment (Bai et al., 2023; van Lengerich et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Isolated HER ectodomains form strong homodimers and only weakly detectable heterodimers in the presence of their cognate growth factors.
source: Further evidence comes from biophysical studies in which isolated HER ectodomains were shown to form strong homodimers and only weakly detectable heterodimers in the presence of their cognate growth factors (Ferguson et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: EGFR forms heterodimers more favorably when stimulated with betacellulin (BTC).
source: However, this is not always the case and EGFR was reported to form heterodimers more favorably when stimulated with another ligand, betacellulin (BTC) (Rush et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: HER4 engages equally as homodimers or as heterodimers with HER2 when interactions between isolated receptor ectodomains were measured.
source: In addition, HER4 seems to engage equally as homodimers or as heterodimers with HER2, at least when interactions between isolated receptor ectodomains were measured (Ferguson et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: HER4 is activated by a diverse set of growth factor ligands including the neuregulin 1–4 family (NRG1-4), amphiregulin, epiregulin (EREG), and BTC.
source: HER4 is activated by a diverse set of growth factor ligands including the neuregulin 1–4 family (NRG1-4), amphiregulin, epiregulin (EREG), and BTC (Plowman et al., 1993; Sweeney et al., 2000; Trenker and Jura, 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: NRG1β plays essential roles in the development and functioning of the cardiovascular system and nervous system.
source: For example, NRG1β plays essential roles in the development and functioning of the cardiovascular system and nervous system (Falls, 2003; Meyer and Birchmeier, 1995), while BTC is implicated in the differentiation of pancreatic β-cells (Dunbar and Goddard, 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: BTC is implicated in the differentiation of pancreatic β-cells.
source: For example, NRG1β plays essential roles in the development and functioning of the cardiovascular system and nervous system (Falls, 2003; Meyer and Birchmeier, 1995), while BTC is implicated in the differentiation of pancreatic β-cells (Dunbar and Goddard, 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: In human T lymphoblastic CEM cells stably expressing HER4, NRG1β and NRG2β are the most potent activators of AKT signaling, while BTC induces the strongest activation of ERK1/2.
source: In the human T lymphoblastic CEM cells stably expressing HER4, NRG1β (and NRG2β) are the most potent activators of AKT signaling, while BTC induces the strongest activation of ERK1/2 (Sweeney et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: BTC appears to be uniquely poised to promote signaling by a wide range of HER heterodimers, including HER2/HER3, EGFR/HER3 and HER2/HER4.
source: In particular, BTC appears to be uniquely poised to promote signaling by a wide range of HER heterodimers, including HER2/HER3 (Dunbar and Goddard, 2000; Graus-Porta et al., 1997; Alimandi et al., 1997), EGFR/HER3 and HER2/HER4 (Rush et al., 2018; Dunbar and Goddard, 2000; Graus-Porta et al., 1997; Alimandi et al., 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Only crystal structures of NRG1β-bound HER4 dimers have been reported.
source: Whether HER4 dimers adopt different conformations while bound to different ligands, as seen in EGFR, has remained an open question as only crystal structures of NRG1β-bound HER4 dimers have been reported (Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: A spectrum of ligand-bound EGFR structures revealed different dimerization interfaces and underscored that the dimerization arm plays an important role in communication between the ligand binding pocket and EGFR dimer interface.
source: A spectrum of ligand-bound EGFR structures, including high-affinity (EGF and TGFα) or low-affinity (EREG), revealed different dimerization interfaces and underscored that the dimerization arm plays an important role in communication between the ligand binding pocket and EGFR dimer interface (Freed et al., 2017; Huang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The HER2/HER4/NRG1β structure was determined at 3.3 Å resolution.
source: Focused data processing on the ectodomains resulted in reconstructions of the NRG1β- and BTC-bound HER2/HER4 heterodimers at 3.3 Å and 4.3 Å resolution, respectively (Figure 1b–c, Figure 1—figure supplement 4 and Figure 1—figure supplement 5, Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the cryo-EM structure determination.

claim: The HER2/HER4/BTC structure was determined at 4.3 Å resolution.
source: Focused data processing on the ectodomains resulted in reconstructions of the NRG1β- and BTC-bound HER2/HER4 heterodimers at 3.3 Å and 4.3 Å resolution, respectively (Figure 1b–c, Figure 1—figure supplement 4 and Figure 1—figure supplement 5, Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the cryo-EM structure determination.

claim: In both HER2/HER4 structures, the ectodomains adopt a characteristic 'heart-shaped' arrangement observed in previously solved structures of liganded HER receptor dimers.
source: In both structures, the ectodomains adopt a characteristic 'heart-shaped' arrangement observed in previously solved X-ray and cryo-EM structures of liganded HER receptor dimers (Garrett et al., 2002; Liu et al., 2012; Ogiso et al., 2002; Diwanji et al., 2021; Bai et al., 2023; Freed et al., 2017; Huang et al., 2021; Lu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: The HER2/HER4/NRG1β structures complete the panel of recently reported HER2 heterodimeric complexes.
source: The HER2/HER4/NRG1β structures complete the panel of recently reported HER2 heterodimeric complexes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: In the HER2/HER4 complexes, the ligand-free HER2 enforces an asymmetric geometry within the heart-shaped ectodomain complex.
source: As in the HER2/HER3/NRG1β, HER2/EGFR/EGF, and HER2/EGFR/EREG structures (Diwanji et al., 2021; Bai et al., 2023), in the HER2/HER4 complexes the ligand-free HER2 enforces an asymmetric geometry within the heart-shaped ectodomain complex (Figure 1b–c, Figure 1—figure supplement 6a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: The conformation adopted by HER2 is nearly identical in all HER2-containing heterodimer complexes.
source: The conformation adopted by HER2 is nearly identical in all complexes (Figure 1—figure supplement 6b, pairwise RMSD within HER2s 1.1–1.6 Å across different complexes), and is the same as observed in structures of an isolated HER2 ectodomain alone or in complex with therapeutic antibodies with only minor variations at the tip of the dimerization arm (Figure 1—figure supplement 6b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figure showing structural comparison.

claim: HER2 does not undergo observable conformational changes upon heterodimerization with other HER receptors.
source: Thus, our structures are consistent with previous findings that HER2 does not undergo observable conformational changes upon heterodimerization with other HER receptors.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from structural analysis.

claim: The conformation adopted by HER4 in the HER2/HER4 structure is identical to a previously observed conformation in the crystal structure of isolated HER4 extracellular domain bound to NRG1β.
source: The conformation adopted by HER4 in our structure is identical to a previously observed conformation in the crystal structure of isolated HER4 extracellular domain bound to NRG1β (RMSD 1.7 Å – 4.4 Å across different structures).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with RMSD values.

claim: The larger-scale domain conformation of the HER2/HER4 heterodimers stabilized by NRG1β and BTC is identical with only small differences in the ligand binding pockets.
source: Despite the diverse sequences of the NRG1β and BTC ligands, the larger-scale domain conformation of the HER2/HER4 heterodimers stabilized by each ligand is identical with only small differences in the ligand binding pockets (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figure.

claim: Extensive 3D variability and 3D classification analysis of the HER2/HER4/NRG1β and HER2/HER4/BTC datasets did not reveal any defined conformational heterogeneity within domains IV or dimerization arm regions.
source: Extensive 3D variability and 3D classification analysis of the HER2/HER4/NRG1β and HER2/HER4/BTC datasets did not reveal any defined conformational heterogeneity within domains IV or dimerization arm regions (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figure showing 3D classification.

claim: HER2 and HER4 heterodimerize mainly via interactions between domains II, with significant contributions from the dimerization arms.
source: Like other HER receptor dimers, HER2 and HER4 heterodimerize mainly via interactions between domains II, with significant contributions from the dimerization arms (Figure 2a–b), which carry conserved sequence features across HER family (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: The total buried surface area (BSA) at the HER2/HER4 heterodimer interface encompasses 2784 Å2.
source: The total buried surface area (BSA) at the HER2/HER4 heterodimer interface (domains I-III, measured using UCSF ChimeraX) encompasses 2784 Å2 and is comparable to HER4 and EGFR homodimers (2768–2866 A2, PDB: 3U7U; 3006 A2, PDB: 3NJP, respectively) and the EGFR/HER2 heterodimer (2864 A2, PDB: 8HGO), while the HER2/HER3 heterodimer interface is significantly smaller (2066 A2, PDB: 7MN5) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figure and specific measurements.

claim: The HER2/HER4 interface has two salt bridges (HER2 H237 – HER4 D218 and HER2 E265 – HER4 R232) compared to only one in HER2/EGFR and none in HER2/HER3.
source: The HER2/HER4 interface has two salt bridges (HER2 H237 – HER4 D218 and HER2 E265 – HER4 R232) compared to only one in HER2/EGFR and none in HER2/HER3 (Figure 2b box A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figure showing interface details.

claim: HER2 and HER4 dimerization arms are resolved in both NRG1β and BTC-bound HER2/HER4 complexes.
source: HER2 and HER4 dimerization arms are resolved in both NRG1β and BTC-bound HER2/HER4 complexes (Figure 1b–c, Figure 2a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: The HER2/HER4 complex is the only HER2 heterodimer that involves domain I of both receptors in the dimer interface via the tip of the dimerization arms in a near-symmetric fashion.
source: The HER2/HER4 complex is the only HER2 heterodimer that involves domain I of both receptors in the dimer interface via the tip of the dimerization arms in a near-symmetric fashion (Figure 2d, Figure 2—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: HER2/HER4 heterodimers are the most stable among HER2 heterodimers.
source: This suggests that HER2/HER4 heterodimers are the most stable among HER2 heterodimers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from structural observations.

claim: Recombinant HER2 and HER4 ECDs form the most stable heterocomplex among all other HER heterodimers, with efficiency similar to HER4 homodimers.
source: Consistent with this notion, previous studies showed that the recombinant HER2 and HER4 ECDs form the most stable heterocomplex among all other HER heterodimers, with efficiency similar to HER4 homodimers (Ferguson et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citation.

claim: The substitution of the HER4 dimerization arm to a GS-arm does not notably affect NRG1β-induced phosphorylation of HER2, HER4, ERK, and AKT relative to receptors featuring wild-type dimerization arm sequences.
source: NRG1β-induced phosphorylation of HER2, HER4, ERK, and AKT was not notably affected by the substitution of the HER4 dimerization arm to a GS-arm relative to receptors featuring wild-type dimerization arm sequences, indicating that the HER4 dimerization arm is not required for assembly and activation of HER2/HER4 heterodimers (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figure showing Western blot data.

claim: The HER4 dimerization arm is not required for assembly and activation of HER2/HER4 heterodimers.
source: NRG1β-induced phosphorylation of HER2, HER4, ERK, and AKT was not notably affected by the substitution of the HER4 dimerization arm to a GS-arm relative to receptors featuring wild-type dimerization arm sequences, indicating that the HER4 dimerization arm is not required for assembly and activation of HER2/HER4 heterodimers (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from experimental data.

claim: The substitution of the HER2 dimerization arm fully abolished the activation of the HER2/HER4 heterocomplex.
source: In contrast, the substitution of the HER2 dimerization arm sequence fully abolished the activation of the heterocomplex, as previously reported (Figure 2e; Bai et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figure and citation.

claim: Despite full engagement at the interface of both dimerization arms in the HER2/HER4 complexes, the HER4 arm is still dispensable for activation, and it is the HER2 arm that potentiates the formation of the active complex.
source: Thus, despite full engagement at the interface of both dimerization arms in the HER2/HER4 complexes, the HER4 arm is still dispensable for activation, and it is the HER2 arm that potentiates the formation of the active complex.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from experimental data.

claim: The final reconstructions of HER4/NRG1β and HER4/BTC used for model building included 205,726 and 274,540 particles and attained a GS-FSC resolution of 3.38 and 3.70 Å with C1 symmetry, respectively.
source: The final reconstructions of HER4/NRG1β and HER4/BTC used for model building included 205,726 and 274,540 particles and attained a GS-FSC resolution of 3.38 and 3.70 Å with C1 symmetry, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the cryo-EM structure determination.

claim: Applying C2 symmetry in the final non-uniform refinement run improved the resolution of HER4 homodimers to 3.26 and 3.49 Å.
source: Applying C2 symmetry in the final non-uniform refinement run improved the resolution to 3.26 and 3.49 Å.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the cryo-EM structure determination.

claim: Liganded HER4 assembles into homodimers with near-perfect C2 symmetry.
source: As observed in a previous HER4/NRG1β crystal structure of isolated ECDs, liganded HER4 assembles into homodimers with near-perfect C2 symmetry (Figure 3a, Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: The HER4/NRG1β and HER4/BTC homodimers adopt overall similar conformations, but the reconstructions show differences in the intermonomer angles.
source: The HER4/NRG1β and HER4/BTC homodimers adopt overall similar conformations, but our reconstructions show differences in the intermonomer angles that are adopted by NRG1β- vs BTC-bound homodimers (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figure.

claim: The two receptors in the HER4/NRG1β dimer adopt an angle of 37 degrees compared to 33 degrees for HER4/BTC.
source: The two receptors in the HER4/NRG1β dimer adopt an angle of 37 degrees compared to 33 degrees for HER4/BTC.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with specific angle measurements.

claim: 3D classification analysis revealed substantial scissor-like movements around the dimerization arm in both HER4/NRG1β and HER4/BTC datasets with the concerted intermonomer movement of domains I and IV, varying from 35 to 39 degrees for HER4/NRG1β and 30–35 degrees for HER4/BTC.
source: Detailed 3D classification analysis revealed substantial scissor-like movements around the dimerization arm in both data sets with the concerted intermonomer movement of domains I and IV, varying from 35 to 39 degrees for HER4/NRG1β and 30–35 degrees for HER4/BTC (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figure showing 3D classification.

claim: The observations of intermonomer angle differences are indicative of the increased dynamics present in homodimeric HER4 receptor assemblies compared to their HER2-bound heterodimer counterparts.
source: Such observations are indicative of the increased dynamics present in homodimeric HER4 receptor assemblies compared to their HER2-bound heterodimer counterparts.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: In the HER4/NRG1β pocket, HER4 K438, K35, E112 and D376 form salt bridges with NRG1β E215, D219, R207 and R220, respectively.
source: In the HER4/NRG1β pocket, HER4 K438, K35, E112 and D376 form salt bridges with NRG1β E215, D219, R207 and R220, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing ligand binding pocket interactions.

claim: In the HER4/BTC pocket, HER4 D376 engages an equivalent BTC R103, but the other three residues are substituted with hydrophobic/polar residues in BTC.
source: In the HER4/BTC pocket, HER4 D376 also engages an equivalent BTC R103, but the other three residues are substituted with hydrophobic/polar residues in BTC (NRG1β E215=BTC G98, NRG1β D219=BTC A102, NRG1β R207=BTC T90) (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figure.

claim: Substitutions into small, apolar residues in BTC result in a more 'compressed' ligand-binding pocket in HER4/BTC homodimers than in HER4/NRG1β homodimers, which may allosterically determine different intermonomer angles via modulation of dimerization arm positioning.
source: Thus, substitutions into small, apolar residues in BTC result in a more 'compressed' ligand-binding pocket in HER4/BTC homodimers than in HER4/NRG1β homodimers, which may allosterically determine different intermonomer angles via modulation of dimerization arm positioning (Figure 3b–e).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of structural observations.

claim: The cryo-EM analysis of full-length HER4 homodimers reveals multiple well-resolved N-linked glycans in receptor ectodomains.
source: Our cryo-EM analysis of full-length HER4 homodimers reveals multiple well-resolved N-linked glycans in receptor ectodomains and points to their role in stabilizing interactions between two receptor monomers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from cryo-EM analysis.

claim: HER4 features 11 known N-glycosylation sites: N138, N174, N181, N253, N358, N410, N473, N495, N548, N576, and N620.
source: HER4 features 11 known N-glycosylation sites (as defined in Uniprot (ID: Q15303): N138, N174, N181, N253, N358, N410, N473, N495, N548, N576, and N620).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Uniprot database.

claim: Eight of the eleven HER4 N-glycosylation sites are resolved in the cryo-EM maps of both HER4/NRG1β and HER4/BTC homodimers that enabled the building of core glycan trees up to 5 sugar moieties.
source: Eight of them are resolved in the cryo-EM maps of both HER4/NRG1β and HER4/BTC homodimers that enabled the building of core glycan trees up to 5 sugar moieties (Figure 4a, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, shown for HER4 /NRG1β).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: The HER4 maps show continuous cryo-EM density connecting the two receptor monomers originating from N548 and N576 on domain IV of one receptor monomer and N358 on domain III of the other receptor involving sugar moieties beyond the core glycan trees.
source: Most remarkably, at lower contour levels, our HER4 maps show continuous cryo-EM density connecting the two receptor monomers originating from N548 and N576 on domain IV of one receptor monomer and N358 on domain III of the other receptor involving sugar moieties beyond the core glycan trees of 4–5 sugars (Figure 4a box D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figures showing glycan density.

claim: The analysis of the HER4/NRG1β homodimer cryo-EM density uncovers an important role of receptor glycosylation in stabilizing the active HER4 monomer by bridging its two distal domains and likely both monomers within the HER4 homodimer through direct inter-receptor connections.
source: Thus, our analysis of the HER4/NRG1β homodimer cryo-EM density uncovers an important role of receptor glycosylation in stabilizing the active HER4 monomer by bridging its two distal domains, domain II and IV and domains I and II, and likely both monomers within the HER4 homodimer through direct inter-receptor connections.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from structural analysis.

claim: In contrast to the HER4 homodimers, continuous density connecting the two heterodimer monomers is not observed in HER2/HER4 heterodimers indicating that glycan-mediated interfaces seen in HER4 homodimers cannot be established in HER2/HER4 heterodimers.
source: However, in contrast to the HER4 homodimers, we do not observe continuous density connecting the two heterodimer monomers indicating that glycan-mediated interfaces seen in HER4 homodimers cannot be established in HER2/HER4 heterodimers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a comparison between homodimers and heterodimers.

claim: HER2 does not have glycosylation consensus sites equivalent to HER4 N358, N548, and N576.
source: This is because HER2 does not have glycosylation consensus sites equivalent to HER4 N358, N548, and N576 (Figure 4b box C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figure.

claim: The higher propensity for HER4 to homodimerize rather than heterodimerize with HER2 observed in pull-downs is at least partially rooted in the stabilization of the homodimer by glycan-mediated interactions.
source: Based on these observations, it is tempting to speculate that the higher propensity for HER4 to homodimerize rather than heterodimerize with HER2 observed in our pull-downs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b) is at least partially rooted in the stabilization of the homodimer by glycan-mediated interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as speculation based on structural observations.

claim: The HER2/HER4 heterodimer structures now complete the ensemble of possible HER receptor heterodimer structures that involve the orphan HER2 receptor.
source: The HER2/HER4 heterodimer structures now complete the ensemble of possible HER receptor heterodimer structures that involve the orphan HER2 receptor.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Only the ectodomains are resolved in the full-length receptor structures, as repeatedly has been the case for any full-length receptor tyrosine kinase reconstructions.
source: Only the ectodomains are resolved in our structures, as repeatedly has been the case for any full-length receptor tyrosine kinase reconstructions (Diwanji et al., 2021; Huang et al., 2021; Nielsen et al., 2022; Li et al., 2019; Uchikawa et al., 2019; Krimmer et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: Interactions contributed by the intracellular domains appear to be essential for the stabilization of the receptor complexes in cryo-EM reconstructions.
source: While not resolved, interactions contributed by the intracellular domains appear to be essential for the stabilization of the receptor complexes in our cryo-EM reconstructions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the need for kinase domain modifications.

claim: Across the HER family, the three HER2-containing heterodimers adopt an asymmetric heart-shaped ectodomain structure and in each one of them the HER2 conformation is identical while the dimerization interface is unique.
source: Across the family, the three HER2-containing heterodimers adopt an asymmetric heart-shaped ectodomain structure and in each one of them the HER2 conformation is identical while the dimerization interface is unique.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of structural findings.

claim: The HER2/HER3 interface is most dynamic with the HER3 dimerization arm not being resolved at all.
source: The HER2/HER3 interface is most dynamic with the HER3 dimerization arm not being resolved at all (Diwanji et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: The HER2/HER4 heterodimer seems to be most stable among HER2-containing heterodimers, as measured by studying associations between isolated HER ectodomains.
source: This binding mode might explain HER2/HER4 heterodimer seems to be most stable among HER2-containing heterodimers, as measured by studying associations between isolated HER ectodomains (Ferguson et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: The overall weaker interactions that HER2 makes with the dimerization arms of its partner receptors are likely the reason why these partner arms are not needed for the stabilization of the active signaling HER2 heterodimers.
source: Lastly, the overall weaker interactions that HER2 makes with the dimerization arms of its partner receptors are likely the reason why these partner arms are not needed for the stabilization of the active signaling HER2 heterodimers.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from structural observations.

claim: Both NRG1β and BTC favor HER4 homo-association, and only a small fraction of complexes purified using pulldowns with these ligands yielded HER2/HER4 heterodimers.
source: We note that both NRG1β and BTC favor HER4 homo-association, and only a small fraction of complexes purified using pulldowns with these ligands immobilized on beads yielded HER2/HER4 heterodimers.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an observation from purification experiments.

claim: Co-expressed EGFR and HER2 receptors stimulated with EGF formed almost exclusively EGFR homodimers upon detergent extraction, with the limited formation of EGFR/HER2 heterodimers.
source: This phenomenon has been previously observed for the EGFR/HER2 system, where co-expressed receptors stimulated with EGF formed almost exclusively EGFR homodimers upon detergent extraction, with the limited formation of EGFR/HER2 heterodimers (Bai et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: Live-cell single molecule imaging of EGFR and HER2 on the plasma membrane of EGFR/HER2 positive SUM159 cells after EGF stimulation showed only a small fraction of heterodimerization (<10%).
source: The same study also reported only a small fraction of heterodimerization (<10%) by live-cell single molecule imaging of EGFR and HER2 on the plasma membrane of EGFR/HER2 positive SUM159 cells after EGF stimulation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: The degree of symmetry between ectodomains of EGFR in the active liganded dimer has been correlated with the strength of its signaling output.
source: The degree of symmetry between ectodomains of EGFR in the active liganded dimer has been correlated with the strength of its signaling output.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as established knowledge.

claim: Low-affinity EGFR ligands (EREG, Epigen) result in asymmetric and dynamic dimers while high-affinity ligands (EGF, TGFα) result in symmetric and stable dimers.
source: Ligand binding is allosterically coupled to the positioning of the dimerization arm and depends on how the ligand engages domains I and III. In EGFR, this allosteric path is differentially engaged by low-affinity EGFR ligands (EREG, Epigen) vs high-affinity ligands (EGF, TGFα), resulting in asymmetric and dynamic dimers vs symmetric and stable dimers, respectively (Garrett et al., 2002; Ogiso et al., 2002; Freed et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: Weak asymmetric EGFR dimers correlate with more sustained activation of ERK and AKT pathways leading to differentiation, while more stable symmetric dimers induce more transient activation resulting in proliferation.
source: The weak asymmetric EGFR dimers have been shown to correlate with more sustained activation of ERK and AKT pathways leading to differentiation, while the more stable symmetric dimers induce more transient activation resulting in proliferation (Freed et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: BTC more efficiently activates the ERK pathway while NRG1β activates the AKT pathway more potently in HER4 homodimers.
source: Specifically, the two high-affinity HER4 ligands BTC and NRG1β were shown to be different, with BTC more efficiently activating the ERK pathway while NRG1β activated the AKT pathway more potently (Sweeney et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: The structures of HER4 ectodomain dimers bound to NRG1β and BTC show notable scissor-like movements around the dimerization arms with different intermonomer angles between the two ligands.
source: Our structures of HER4 ectodomain dimers bound to NRG1β and BTC presented here show that in both homodimers there are notable scissor-like movements around the dimerization arms with different intermonomer angles between the two ligands.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of structural findings.

claim: It is possible that different dimer conformations of HER4 homodimers influence the stability and consequently signaling outputs emanating from these complexes.
source: It is possible that these different dimer conformations influence the stability and consequently signaling outputs emanating from these HER4 homodimers.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation.

claim: BTC and NRG1β complexes with the HER2/HER4 heterodimers showed no discernable structural differences.
source: In contrast to the effects that BTC or NRG1β have on stabilizing more diverse conformational ensembles of the HER4 homodimers, their complexes with the HER2/HER4 heterodimers showed no discernable structural differences.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a comparison.

claim: In the HER2/EGFR heterodimer, high-affinity EGF and low-affinity EREG failed to stabilize different dimer conformations.
source: Strikingly in the HER2/EGFR heterodimer, an even more diverse set of growth factors: high-affinity EGF and low-affinity EREG, also failed to stabilize different dimer conformations (Bai et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: EGFR and HER4 receptors sample a wider selection of active homodimer states that can be exploited by different ligands and might be better conduits for ligand-specific signaling responses than their respective HER2 heterodimers.
source: Altogether, these structural analyses show that EGFR and HER4 receptors sample a wider selection of active homodimers states that can be exploited by different ligands and might be better conduits for ligand-specific signaling responses that their respective HER2 heterodimers.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from structural analyses.

claim: N-linked glycosylation of receptor tyrosine kinases plays a crucial role in their maturation, stability, and regulation of their interaction with ligands, the extracellular matrix and other membrane proteins.
source: N-linked glycosylation of receptor tyrosine kinases plays a crucial role in their maturation, stability, and regulation of their interaction with ligands, the extracellular matrix and other membrane proteins (Duarte et al., 2022; Contessa et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: Aberrant glycosylation patterns of HER receptors have been associated with diseases such as cancer and promoting drug resistance.
source: HER receptors are heavily glycosylated and their aberrant glycosylation patterns have been associated with diseases such as cancer and promoting drug resistance (Zhen et al., 2003; Rodrigues et al., 2021; Britain et al., 2018; Peiris et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: A mutation of the N418 glycosylation site on HER3 promotes its ligand-independent association with HER2.
source: For example, a mutation of the N418 glycosylation site on HER3 promotes its ligand-independent association with HER2 (Yokoe et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: Mutation of N579 on EGFR drives its ligand-independent activation as well as increases its affinity for ligands.
source: Likewise, mutation of N579 on EGFR drives its ligand-independent activation as well as increases its affinity for ligands (Whitson et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: The cryo-EM maps of HER4 homodimers and HER2/HER4 heterodimers offer the first glimpse into extensive glycan-mediated contacts in an active HER receptor dimer.
source: To our knowledge, the cryo-EM maps of HER4 homodimers and HER2/HER4 heterodimers offer the first glimpse into extensive glycan-mediated contacts in an active HER receptor dimer.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a claim about novelty.

claim: The particularly strong propensity for HER4 homodimerization over heterodimerization with HER2 is, at least partially, rooted in the missing glycan-mediated stabilization of the heterodimer.
source: It is tempting to speculate that the particularly strong propensity for HER4 homodimerization over heterodimerization with HER2 that we see in our reconstitution experiments is, at least partially, rooted in the missing glycan-mediated stabilization of the heterodimer.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation.

claim: MD simulations on HER4/EGFR heterodimer models suggested that glycans present on HER4 N358 and N548, as well as EGFR N361, form a connection in the dimerization interface that effectively stabilizes the heterodimer.
source: Most recently, MD simulations conducted on the HER4/EGFR heterodimer models have suggested that the glycans present on HER4 N358 and N548, as well as EGFR N361 (which is equivalent to HER4 N358), form a connection in the dimerization interface that effectively stabilizes the heterodimer (Motamedi et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: The current study provides the first direct experimental evidence that glycan interactions are operative at the level of HER4 homodimers.
source: Our current study provides the first direct experimental evidence that these glycan interactions are operative at the level of HER4 homodimers.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: Inter-receptor glycans appear in EGFR homodimers between N361 and the more membrane-proximal N603.
source: Moreover, we analyzed the published EGFR cryo-EM maps (Huang et al., 2021) and noticed that the inter-receptor glycans also appear in EGFR homodimers between N361 and the more membrane-proximal N603.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: The analysis points to an important role, and potential conserved mechanisms by which glycosylation contributes to the HER dimer interfaces.
source: Altogether, our analysis points to an important role, and potential conserved mechanisms by which glycosylation contributes to the HER dimer interfaces (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c–d).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the analysis.

claim: The structural analysis provides new knowledge on HER receptor activation by their different growth factor ligands and mechanistic distinctions of their homodimeric versus heterodimeric pairings.
source: In summary, our structural analysis provides new knowledge on HER receptor activation by their different growth factor ligands and mechanistic distinctions of their homodimeric versus heterodimeric pairings.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of contributions.

claim: The findings reveal a greater aptitude of HER homodimers to differentiate between biased agonists, at least as compared to HER2-containing heterodimers.
source: Through this, our findings reveal a greater aptitude of HER homodimers to differentiate between biased agonists, at least as compared to HER2-containing heterodimers.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the findings.

claim: The structures for the first time reveal extensive intra and interdomain glycan contacts at the active HER dimer interface.
source: Our structures for the first time reveal extensive intra and interdomain glycan contacts at the active HER dimer interface and have the potential to further understanding of how glycosylation can be leveraged for the design of better HER-targeted therapeutics, and how it can contribute to drug resistance.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of contributions.

claim: The active HER2/HER4 heterodimer was only reconstituted in the HER4 activator (IQ)/ HER2 receiver (VR) configuration, pointing to stereotyped roles that these two receptors play in the active complex irrespective of the activating growth factor.
source: Strikingly, the active heterodimer was only reconstituted in the HER4 activator (IQ)/ HER2 receiver (VR) configuration pointing to stereotyped roles that these two receptors play in the active complex irrespective of the activating growth factor (Figure 1a, Figure 1—figure supplement 1f).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figure showing Western blot data.

claim: HER2/HER4 dimers constituted only a small fraction of complexes purified using both NRG1β and BTC ligands, indicating that in each case HER4 favored self-association.
source: We observed that HER2/HER4 dimers constituted only a small fraction of complexes purified using both ligands, indicating that in each case HER4 favored self-association (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b + 1d).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to figures showing purification data.
